title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the start of chapter VI, 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', dated 18 June 1986. Grothendieck is axiomatizing an 'algèbre de figures' or 'atelier'. It is a preliminary combinatorial structure, out of which a 'contrée' (a tame space with a chosen family of multistrata) is to be built. The previous page says the multistrata play a role like a generating family of open sets for a topology, or a generating family in a topos.

Data from the previous page: three sets, L (lieux), M (multistrates) and F (figures), with injections L ⊂ M ⊂ F (1.2).

This page adds two further maps (1.3).
(a) An injection F → P(M), F ↦ F̃ = Dépl(F), the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of F. This is the set of multistrata incident to F. Equivalently, it is an incidence relation between M and F: X is incident to F (X is a 'strate de la figure F') iff X ∈ F̃.
(b) A map F → Fig(M) ⊂ P(P(M)). Here Fig(M) is the set of 'figures ensemblistes' in M, i.e. families of subsets of M. The map is F ↦ Fig_M(F) = { X̃ : X ∈ F̃ } (1.4).

Map (b) is deduced from (a) together with M ⊂ F. Every multistratum X, seen as a figure, has its own unfolding X̃. So F is represented by the family of unfoldings of its incident multistrata. Grothendieck states that the axioms will make this a set-theoretic figure in M, faithfully indexed by F̃.

Anticipated structure:
- M carries a partial order ≤.
- Each F̃ is a closed subset of M, i.e. down-closed: closed for the Alexandrov-type topology of the poset.
- For a multistratum X, X̃ = { Y ∈ M : Y ≤ X } is the principal down-set (1.5).

Modern reading:
- M is the incidence (face) poset of a stratification; ≤ means 'is contained in the closure of'.
- A figure is identified with the closed union of strata it contains, i.e. a down-set of the strata poset.
- Fig_M(F) is the 'cell-complex' presentation: each stratum is replaced by its closure, the set of its faces.
- Faithful indexation follows from antisymmetry, since X ↦ ↓X is injective on a poset.

The next page warns that the figure attached to X is ↓X, not {X}. It identifies M → F_ferm(M), X ↦ ↓X.

Purpose: set-up toward the 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) programme of the Esquisse. Spaces are to be described combinatorially through strata, their incidence order and closed unions of strata.
errors: Minor terminological slip: the text alternates between 'multistructures' and 'multistrates' (and 'struct.' for 'strate'); the intended notion is clearly multistrata.

Injectivity of F → P(M) and the claim that Fig_M(F) is a set-theoretic figure faithfully indexed by F̃ are only asserted as consequences of axioms not yet stated. Faithfulness needs ≤ to be antisymmetric, which is fine for an order relation.
The note '(b) se déduit de a) et de 1.2 a)' is correct as a definition, but the injectivity of (b) is marked with '?' and is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'algebra of figures' / 'atelier' with three sorts (places, multistrata, figures) and inclusions L⊂M⊂F, as foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial axiomatization of stratified spaces (cf. o-minimal / tame stratifications, abstract stratified sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tame topology programme: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces tame topology, but not this axiomatics

ideas.what: Incidence relation between multistrata and figures; 'déploiement' F̃ = set of incident multistrata
ideas.modern_name: set of strata of a closed stratified subspace; incidence relation

ideas.what: Order on multistrata with X̃ = ↓X and figures as closed (down-closed) subsets
ideas.modern_name: face/incidence poset of a stratification with its Alexandrov topology; principal down-sets as closures of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937); face posets of regular CW complexes (Björner); exit-path/poset-stratified spaces (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie HA App. A)

ideas.what: Representing a figure as a 'figure ensembliste' Fig_M(F) = {↓X : X ∈ F̃} ⊂ P(P(M)), i.e. a family of subsets faithfully indexed by its strata
ideas.modern_name: presentation of a cell complex by closures of cells (abstract cell complex / face lattice representation)

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins a three-sorted axiomatic foundation ('atelier': lieux, multistrates, figures) for tame topology. The 'contrée' is to be obtained from a chosen generating family of multistrata, analogously to a generating family of a topos. This is a concrete unpublished attempt at the foundations promised in the Esquisse's tame topology section. Its relation to later poset-stratified/exit-path frameworks is unexplored.
missed.quote: on pose Fig_M(F) = {X̃ | X ∈ F̃ = Dépl(F)} ⊂ P(M) ... M sera muni d'une relation d'ordre ≤ ... X̃ = {Y ∈ M | Y ≤ X}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Tame/stratified homotopy theory (poset-stratified spaces, exit-path ∞-categories, o-minimal homotopy) is active. Grothendieck's intended axioms could be compared with these frameworks, though this page itself is only basic set-up.

deep.surprise_reason: This page is foundational bookkeeping. It sets up an incidence relation and the poset of strata with principal down-sets as closures, which is natural and standard in content. Its interest is mainly historical, as the opening of an unpublished 1986 axiomatization of tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'la multistruct. X est incidente' should read 'la multistrate X est incidente'; 'c'est une struct. de figure F' is likely 'c'est une strate de la figure F'.
'toute élément X de M (i.e. multistruct.)' should read 'tout élément X de M (i.e. multistrate)'.
The marginal annotation under the arrow in (1.3 b), transcribed '[injective][?]', is illegible ('sur seul...'?); uncertain.
Last line: 'X̃ [?] aura (1.5)' is probably 'on aura (1.5)'.
